title: EC-Council ECIH
summary: EC-Council ECIH is a professional certification offered by EC-Council. This independent study guide covers all 10 course modules: Introduction to Incident Handling and Response, Incident Handling and Response Process, First Response, Handling and Responding to Malware Incidents, Handling and Responding to Email Security Incidents, Handling and Responding to Network Security Incidents, Handling and Responding to Web Application Security Incidents, Handling and Responding to Cloud Security Incidents, Handling and Responding to Insider Threats, Handling and Responding to Endpoint Security Incidents. Every module has a MEDIUM and a HARD scenario exam, written as realistic workplace situations rather than recall questions, so you practise applying each module the way the job asks for it.

beginner.definition: The ECIH is a certification from EC-Council about incident handling. Incident handling means the steps you follow when a company is attacked or a system breaks its security rules. The exam tests whether you know how to prepare for attacks and how to respond when they happen. It sits between entry level training and specialist forensics work.
beginner.whyItMatters: Every company needs people who stay calm when a security alarm fires. This certification shows an employer that you understand a structured response process and not just a list of tools. It helps you move from a support desk role into a security operations centre. It also gives you a shared language for working with managers and lawyers during a real breach. The exam is well known, so recruiters recognise it on a CV.
howItWorks: Start by learning the vocabulary. Learn what an event, an incident and a breach mean, because the exam uses these words precisely.
Study the incident handling lifecycle as a loop. It runs from preparation through identification, containment, eradication, recovery and lessons learned.
Work through the attack categories in the syllabus. They include malware, email attacks, web attacks and network attacks.
Practise on a home lab. Follow a written runbook and write a short incident report for each exercise you finish.
Review the official exam blueprint. Book the exam when your practice scores are steady rather than lucky.
The exam itself is a proctored knowledge test. It uses multiple choice questions, including scenario items about a described incident.
beginner.example: Picture a finance team member who opens an email attachment at nine in the morning. By lunchtime, files on a shared drive are renamed. A pop up on the screen then demands payment. An incident handler does not simply delete the email. First they confirm what happened. Next they stop the spread by isolating the machine and remove the harmful software. Then they restore clean files from backup. Finally they write down what worked, so the next case is faster. That ordered thinking is what the ECIH exam measures.
takeaways: Learn the vocabulary first, because the exam grades precise wording.
Write a practice runbook and an incident report, not just study notes.
Check the current EC-Council blueprint before you book a date.
